problem: Suppose $X$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(X)=55.$ The matrix $Y$ is obtained from $X$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{5}↔{R}_{3}$ (switching the fifth and the third rows). What is the value of $det(Y)?$
worked_solution:
Since swapping any two rows changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite sign, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =-det(X) \\  & =-(55) \\  & =-55.\end{aligned}
$$
